C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A.Summary:
Step (2) of the maintainer's `D40` sequence, and the bundle that pays the live finding `F228` and the two staged findings `F277` and `F278`. It is the `D27` successor of `C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-1-464041EE`: the predecessor's dogfood wrote `D40`'s resolving `CodifiedIn` mid-execution, and the record validator refused `decision-eligible-still-live` from that task to the close (`F278`), so the codify write moves to the close, still the verb's. Build the **record flush/mint verb**: one `bun`-invoked transaction that reads `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`, writes the selected findings and decisions, their index `Entry` lines, the charter row and the four live roots through the shipped canonical serializer, with `--retire`, `--rewrite-roots`, `--stamp-paid-by` and `--split` as its siblings. It ends the hand flush — three bundles this week each wrote a throwaway flush script, no two alike, and the record-schema spec's "the next flush goes through the verb" sentence is the thing this bundle retires. The verb is a `--flush` mode of the record engine in `scripts/` (`D40`'s ruling: the record is this repository's governance meta-artifact, not a shipped capability; no `src/` production write). This bundle is the first verb flush: its own row is written by `--flush` at execution, and `D40`'s `CodifiedIn` is written by the same verb's **codify-only invocation** at the close, not by hand.
**Also in scope, because the verb's refusal set forces one and this authoring run measured the other:** the engine refuses a duplicate entry id and a wrong index `Entry` layer. `F228` measured 2026-09-11 that the shape check does not forbid a duplicate id and `--retire` misdiagnoses one as a missing `layer` attribute. Re-measured 2026-09-17 at `5d9a5c89a4b6e57999051e169c89d36570e4081d`: a duplicate live `<Finding id="f1">` planted in a record copy validates `ok` (exit 0), and `--retire` on a copy with a duplicate live eligible id exits 1 through `setEntryLayer`'s "no readable layer attribute". Separately, the newly staged `F277` measures that a live finding's index `Entry` flipped to `layer="retired"`, with the finding unmoved, also validates `ok` and relieves the index budget at `--rewrite-roots` (`base` 265→264, `headroom` 31→32). The verb's own refusals ("an id already in either layer", "an entry's `layer` agrees with its holding file") prevent new instances; the at-rest record is still silently unguarded, so the validator, `--retire` and `--flush` each gain the named checks. The staged `F278` is this supersede's own finding: a spec named a mechanism (`--codify`) without reading the ruling that fixes its timing, and the draft plan could comply only by taking the record validator off the task boundary.
**Minted 2026-09-17** as the `D27` successor of `C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-1-464041EE` at `d645f8d` (the supersede commit; the predecessor and its driven draft plan moved to `.ngrace/changes/archive/` — 115 archive directories now), with `bun ./src/grace.ts spec new --supersedes C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-1-464041EE --timestamp 2026-09-17T05:45:35Z --path .`; printed path `.ngrace/changes/active/C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A/spec.xml`; printed lines `mint: C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A slug=RECORD-FLUSH-VERB lineage=2 hash=6BB9DF5A branch=c-record-flush-verb timestamp=2026-09-17T05:45:35.000Z` and `mint-search: 1 active, 0 archive prior bundle(s) share slug RECORD-FLUSH-VERB` — whose value half, `1 active, 0 archive`, is this bundle's dogfood `--mint-search` input, carried verbatim because a recomputed count is not the mint-time fact. C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A.Problem:
**No verb writes the record.** `D40` (live in `rulings.xml`, "not yet built") fixes the sequence by dependency: (1) a shape schema and a canonical serializer, shipped by `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E` (`scripts/record-serialize.ts`; every XML record write routes through one `writeRecordXml` that refuses a schema violation and serializes canonically); (2) the flush/mint verb, this bundle; (2b) `spec edit`/`plan edit` and a graph-module verb under `src/`; (3) a lint rule generalising `D1.3`. Between (1) and this bundle the flush is still a hand write: `C-TEACH-CLOSE-DRIVES-PINS-1-B0BC7FBD`'s T-001 selected eight entries from the buffer by anchor id, cut each `---` separator, rendered each `<Finding>` through `serializeRecordDocument`, appended eight index `Entry` lines, ran `--rewrite-roots`, minted the row by hand with its `Charter` and `StatusText`, extended the `bundleMinted` payer table and added two hand-written invariant walks. No two of the last three flushes structured that script the same way.
**The lineage, and why this supersede.** `F278` (staged by this supersede, now this bundle's) records that the approved predecessor spec had the flush write `D40`'s resolving `CodifiedIn` mid-execution, against the shipped one-wave rule. A resolving `CodifiedIn` makes a live decision eligible at once: the validator reports `decision-eligible-still-live` and `validate:ci` reds on the production tree from that task until the close. The rule is archived — `C-APPLY-VERB`'s plan: "Do not write CodifiedIn on D37 (after a resolving CodifiedIn a live Decision is immediately decision-eligible; decision-eligible-still-live fails a task boundary that holds that tree; the close writes the element and --retire in one wave)" — and `D37`'s `CodifiedIn` was written in the close commit (`17d8b47`). The predecessor's draft plan complied by excluding the record suite and the validator from `TargetAssertions` and from two tasks' `Verification`: an instrument routed around the boundary it exists to guard. This successor keeps the one-wave rule — the execution flush writes the findings and the row only, and the verb's codify-only invocation writes `D40`'s `CodifiedIn` at the close, immediately before `apply` and `--retire`.
**The writes the verb must own are pinned by shipped code, and the writers are private.** Measured 2026-09-17 at `5d9a5c89a4b6e57999051e169c89d36570e4081d`: `main()` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1769`) resolves exactly four modes — `--split`, `--retire`, `--stamp-paid-by`, `--rewrite-roots` — and no mode is `--flush`; `renderFinding` (`:427`), `renderDecision` (`:437`), `renderRow` (`:446`) and `writeRecordXml` (`:643`) are module-private, so a sibling script cannot route a record write through the one canonical path without exporting them; `parseFrozenMarkdown` (`:182`) already reads the buffer by anchor id and returns each entry's `headingLine`, `bodyRaw` and `bodyHash` with the separator tail trimmed by `stripBodySeparator` (`:128`); `derivePayerMap` (`:370`) already derives a finding's payer from a registry row's `Pays` once the row's name is an archive directory; `rewriteRecordRoots` (`:1325`) is the only sanctioned root writer and refuses (`ceiling-exceeded`, `missing-ceiling`) rather than raising a ceiling.
**`F228` is live and is the same surface.** `F228` (live in `findings.xml`) records that a duplicate live finding id crashes `--retire` in `setEntryLayer` with a message that names the wrong cause, and that the shape check's silence on duplicate ids is the gap `F207` recorded from the schema side. `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2` paid `F207` by declaring the per-element shape but not the cross-element uniqueness; re-measured here, a duplicate id still validates `ok` and still throws the wrong message, so `F228` is history only in the sense that its text is exact.
**`F277` is the same validator-silence class, one invariant over, and this authoring run measured it.** On a whole-record copy, flipping one live finding's index line from `layer="live"` to `layer="retired"` while `findings.xml` is untouched validates `record-retirement: ok` (exit 0), and `--rewrite-roots` then persists index `base="264" headroom="32" ceiling="296"` against the control's `base="265" headroom="31"` — a hand edit that moves an index line to the retired layer without moving the entry relieves the index budget while the record stays green. No shipped check compares an `Entry`'s `layer` to its holding genre element: `checkStatusFile` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1610`) runs for `Finding`/`Decision`/`Row` only, `recordSchemaViolations` (`scripts/record-serialize.ts:157`) is per-element, `validate-citation-anchors.ts:124` checks index id-duplication and the inventory relation but not `layer`, and `prove-record-preservation.ts` checks inventory ids, tokens and body hashes but not `layer`. The shipped per-bundle "index `Entry` layer agreeing" walks cover only the ids each flush names.
**What is deliberately unchanged.** The buffer is read, never written: entries are pruned only after the flush PR merges, and the pruning stays the authority's post-merge act. The record engine stays under `scripts/` and no `src/` production file changes (`D40`'s boundary and `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2`'s constraint). No ceiling is raised. `README.md` and `examples/` are unchanged (no user-visible surface). Escaping of markup in XML artifacts is mandatory character-data form (`<`, `>`, `&`), never paraphrased brackets.

Goals.Goal: Add a `--flush` mode to `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` that performs the whole record flush in one transaction: read `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`; select staged entries by anchor id (never by position); write each selected finding and decision, its index `Entry` and the charter row; support a **codify-only invocation** (no `--finding`/`--decision`/`--all`, the bundle's row already live) that writes one `CodifiedIn` through the same transaction and holds the roots, so `D40`'s `CodifiedIn` is written at the close with the bundle still under `.ngrace/changes/active/`; and hold every live root (base re-derived from the shipped metric read back, persisted ceiling byte-for-byte, headroom the remainder) — every write through `writeRecordXml`, so the record is canonical at rest. The verb is invoked as `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --flush docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` and named by the `package.json` script `record:flush`. The engine's writers stay module-private: the mode lives in the engine, and no record write path is exported outside it.

The tool owns identity and state, the agent authors prose. The tool owns the entry selection, the id, `status`, `genre`, the index `Entry`, the row's name (the `--change` bundle id, checked against `.ngrace/changes/active/`), the `Charter`'s form (the `mint-search:` line, composed from the `--mint-search` input and the author half), `Pays`, the root attributes and the bytes. The agent supplies the `Charter`'s author half, its `mint-search:` **value** (pasted from `spec new`'s stdout), and the `StatusText` — and the tool refuses a `Charter` that names an `F` token, a `StatusText` that names an `F` token, and a `StatusText` carrying a `Closed with` sentence.

Refusals refuse, with named codes, before any write: `flush-id-absent` (an id absent from the buffer), `flush-id-duplicate` (an id already present in either layer, or twice in the buffer), `flush-row-not-active` (`--change` is not a directory under `.ngrace/changes/active/`), `flush-row-exists` (entries selected while the `--change` row is already live — the codify-only shape is a run with no entries against an existing row, and any other selection against it refuses), `flush-pays-unknown` (a `Pays` token that is neither a flushed `F` token nor a live finding's token), `flush-charter-f-token`, `flush-status-text-f-token`, `flush-status-closed-with`, `flush-codify-absent` (the decision named by `--codify` is absent), `flush-codify-exists` (that decision already carries a resolving `CodifiedIn`), `flush-mint-search-malformed` (a `--mint-search` value not shaped `<n> active, <n> archive`), and the serializer's `record-schema-*` violations and `--rewrite-roots`'s `ceiling-exceeded` / `missing-ceiling`. Each is driven in both directions on a throwaway copy: the clean direction passes, a planted violation reddens with exit non-zero and no byte changed.

The transaction is all-or-nothing: all four next-documents (findings, rulings, index, registry) and their root snapshots are built and schema-validated in memory, ceilings checked, and only then written. A refused run leaves the four files byte-identical, proved by planting a failure (a schema violation and a `Pays` breach) on a copy and comparing bytes before and after.

Pay `F228`, `F277` and `F278`. **`F278`:** the execution flush writes the findings and the row only and the validator stays green at every task boundary; the codify-only invocation writes `D40`'s `CodifiedIn` at the close, immediately before `apply` and `--retire`, so the one-wave rule holds and the write is still the verb's (`D40`). The two validator-silence invariants this bundle's refusals already encode ride with it. **`F228`:** the shipped validator reports a duplicate entry id across either genre pair with a named code and exits non-zero, and `--retire` refuses a duplicate id before any write with a message naming the duplicate rather than a missing `layer` attribute. **`F277`:** the shipped validator reports an index `Entry` whose `layer` disagrees with the file holding its genre element, and `--retire` refuses it before any write. Both directions are driven on copies: the production record stays green, a planted duplicate or a planted layer flip reddens the validator, and `--retire` on each planted violation exits non-zero before any write — for the duplicate, instead of throwing through `setEntryLayer`.

Dogfood, in two waves. **At execution** the flush writes the findings and the row only: `--flush --change C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A --finding F277 --finding F278 --pays "F228 F277 F278" --mint-search "1 active, 0 archive"` writes `F277` and `F278` into `findings.xml`, one index `Entry` each, and the live `registry.xml` row, and holds the roots — with no `--codify`, so the shipped validator stays green at every task boundary. **At the close**, with the bundle still under `active/`, the verb's codify-only invocation writes `D40`'s `CodifiedIn`: `--flush --change C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A --codify D40:test-suite:scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts --mint-search "1 active, 0 archive"`, then `ngrace apply` and `--retire` run in one wave (`C-APPLY-VERB`'s rule), the `--retire` retiring `F228`, `F277`, `F278`, `D40` and the row (`moved 5`). `D40` is codified with `kind="test-suite"` on the verb's suite (`D37`'s precedent: the bundle that built one step of a multi-step ruling codified it, even though the credential model stayed unbuilt). `F270` is selected by no flag and stays staged. The verb's suite extends the `bundleMinted` payer table with `F228`, `F277` and `F278` for its own tokens, as every flush has.

Name the new writer where the record's writers are described. `CLAUDE.md`'s record paragraph and `docs/plans/README.md`'s record paragraph each gain one sentence naming the `--flush` writer beside `--retire`; every token `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` asserts of those two files (`--retire`, "index Entry layers flip in place", "the index has no retired sibling", `decisions.md`, `decisions.xml`, findings/decisions/registry/index/live/retired, "re-derives PaidBy", "never raised", "resolving CodifiedIn", "a resolving TaughtIn does not move it") stays present.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier **T3 (architectural)**: a new writer subsystem under `scripts/` — a new verb mode, a new all-or-nothing transaction, new refusal paths, a shared duplicate-id check, and the record it writes. The skill's T3 row is met by the new subsystem and the new write contract (`D40`'s "a governed XML document is written by a verb or not at all"); no `src/` production file changes and no version surface moves. Roadmap `RM-GOVERNED-PATH`.

Binding rulings carried, not re-derived. **`D40`** fixes the sequence and rules the engine lives in `scripts/` (`validate-record-retirement.ts` or a helper module beside it), with no `src/` production write; this bundle is step (2). **`D27`** — approved artifacts are repaired only by `ngrace supersede`; drafts are revised in place, and this spec is a draft. **`D30`** — the record freezes for the lifetime of a bundle that measures it, and no hard `Constraint` here transcribes a scalar count of a file it changes; every occupancy and root figure lives in `Assumptions` and expires. **`D31`** — the retired sibling is a layer. **`D28`/`D28.1`** — no ceiling is raised: the flush holds the persisted ceiling byte-for-byte and refuses when a live metric exceeds it. **`D39`** — the anti-occupancy guard on ceilings is untouched. **`D37`** — the precedent for codifying one step of a multi-step ruling (`C-APPLY-VERB` codified `D37` while the credential model stayed unbuilt) is the reason `D40` is codified here rather than at step (3).

The vehicle, decided from the write path. `--flush` is a mode of `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, beside `--retire`/`--rewrite-roots`/`--stamp-paid-by`/ `--split`. Every record write must stay behind the module-private `writeRecordXml`; a sibling script would force exporting that writer (and the three renderers) to widen the engine's surface for no gain, and `D40` names the engine file or a helper module beside it. The verb is invoked as `bun …`, never `ngrace …` (the product CLI is `src/`, out of scope). `package.json` gains `"record:flush": "bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --flush"`, and the existing `validate:record-retirement` and `validate:ci` script texts are not changed (they must not contain a mutating mode — `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:386`-387 asserts this).

The verb's inputs, split by `D40`. **Selection:** repeatable `--finding F277` and `--decision D40`, matched by anchor id against the buffer's `` forms, never by position; `--all` flushes every staged entry. The default is no entries: a run with no entries against an **absent** row is a row-only flush, and a run with no entries against an **existing live** row is the **codify-only** invocation — it neither re-mints nor duplicates that row (a run that selects entries while the `--change` row is already live refuses `flush-row-exists`). `F270` (staged, not this bundle's) is selected by no flag and is untouched. **Row:** the row's name is the `--change` bundle id, checked against `.ngrace/changes/active/`; `kind` is `chartered`; `Number` is empty. **`Pays`:** defaults to the flushed `F` tokens in buffer order; `--pays "F228 F277"` overrides and may name a flushed token or a live finding's token, so a flushed finding may be **unpaid** (the `F270` precedent) and a live finding may be paid (`F228`). **`Charter`:** the `mint-search:` value is a mint-time fact and is therefore an **input**, pasted from `spec new`'s stdout as `--mint-search "1 active, 0 archive"` (the two counts only, no prefix and no slug). The tool validates its shape against `/^[0-9]+ active, [0-9]+ archive$/` and refuses a malformed one with `flush-mint-search-malformed`; it owns only the **form**, composing `mint-search: prior bundle(s) share slug ` (the slug derived from the row name), then `, ` and the author's half supplied as `--charter`. The count is never recomputed at flush time: the mint counts prior active and archive bundles by scanning the changes directories, and that helper is module-private to `src/grace-generate.ts`, so reaching it from `scripts/` would be a `src/` production edit that `AC-NO-SRC` and `D40`'s boundary forbid; a supersede or an archive between the mint and the flush would also change a recomputed count. **`StatusText`:** `--status-text`. **`--codify`:** `--codify ::` (e.g. `--codify D40:test-suite:scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`) appends one `` to that decision, resolving by the shipped rule (`test-suite` path exists, `lint-rule` catalog code emittable); with no entries and an existing live `--change` row it is the **codify-only invocation**, which writes that one element through the same validate-then-write transaction, holds the roots and re-mints nothing. **Buffer:** read whole, never written. **Outputs:** the verb prints the flushed ids, the row name and `Pays` (and, for the codify-only invocation, the decision it codified).

The transaction and the roots. All four next-documents are built in memory, each checked by `assertRecordSchema`, every live root's base re-derived from the shipped metric read back (`newlineCount` of the whole file for findings and rulings, the live `Row` count for the registry, the live `Entry` count for the index), each persisted ceiling held byte-for-byte via the `--rewrite-roots` splice, and only then written through `writeRecordXml`. The choice is **validate-then-write**, not temp-and-rename: every refusal is computed before the write loop, so a refused run writes nothing; the proof is a planted schema violation and a planted `Pays` breach on a copy, each leaving all four files byte-identical. A ceiling breach refuses (`ceiling-exceeded`); raising a persisted ceiling is never the remedy (`D39`).

`F228`'s and `F277`'s remedy, on the same engine surface. One shared structural check over the two findings layers, the two rulings layers and the index is consumed by the validator (findings `record-duplicate-id` and `record-index-layer-mismatch`, exit non-zero), by `--retire` (each refusal printed with the id and exit non-zero, **before any write**, never `setEntryLayer`'s "no readable layer attribute"), and by `--flush` (`flush-id-duplicate` and `flush-index-layer-mismatch`). The checks are relations — "an id occurs at most once across its genre's pair", and "every `Entry`'s `layer` equals the layer of the file holding its genre element" — and pin no count. The production record satisfies both (203 live findings, 0 duplicate ids, 0 index layer disagreements measured 2026-09-17); a copy with a planted duplicate or a planted layer flip does not.

Write scope, anchors and modules — enumerated once (`F136.1`'s rule; no second module list anywhere in this artifact). Evidence hygiene. The byte-invariance baseline is the full base commit `5d9a5c89a4b6e57999051e169c89d36570e4081d` (`F210`'s rule: the base-less diff form cannot fail). `git diff` sees tracked paths only (`F174`); the record moves by design and is enumerated here, so no "record unmoved" criterion is written. Every `CloseEvidence` command is evaluated in the applied-archive state (`F196`) and additionally driven inside a faithful whole-repository copy before and after these criteria were written: `Command` exits are read directly, never through a pipe. Every criterion states a relation and pins no projected figure; any occupancy or root number lives in `Assumptions`. Structural counts come from the shipped parser, never `grep -c`. Any test the later plan adds that walks the real repository or the real archive runs under `bun run test` (`bun test --timeout=0`); no per-test timeout number is pinned (`C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2-7AD2A006`), and the CI job's `timeout-minutes` is the only ceiling. Any new finding this authoring run raises is staged in `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` under the next free number (`F279` and following) and reported under `AMBIGUITIES`.

Known boundary, stated rather than hidden. (1) `D40`'s steps (2b) (`spec edit`/`plan edit` and a graph-module verb under `src/`) and (3) (the lint rule generalising `D1.3`) are not this bundle; codifying `D40` here retires it, and later bundles cite it retired. (2) The flush writes the record's four live genre files and the index, but the *canonical-at-rest* property is the serializer's, shipped by `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2`; this bundle adds no new canonical form. (3) The duplicate-id check covers genre pairs (findings findings/retired, rulings rulings/retired); the index-layer check covers every `Entry` against its holding genre element, but the index `Entry` *presence* relation (an id with no `Entry`, or an `Entry` with no id) is `validate-citation-anchors.ts`'s and `prove-record-preservation.ts`'s. (4) `--pays` accepting a live finding's token is what lets a bundle pay a finding it did not stage; the eligibility decision remains the shipped one (a payer's name becomes an archive directory only at the close). (5) A row-only flush (no staged entries) is legal; this bundle's dogfood flushes `F277` and `F278` at execution (its row's `Pays` also names the live `F228`) and codifies `D40` at the close. (6) The codify-only invocation is a parameterization of the existing `--flush` mode, not a second mode, a second writer, or a change to `--retire`'s eligibility.

NonGoals.NonGoal: `README.md` and `examples/` are byte-identical to this spec's base commit `5d9a5c89a4b6e57999051e169c89d36570e4081d`. Owner: unchanged; no user-visible surface — the verb is a `scripts/` meta-artifact of this repository's governance and never a shipped `ngrace` command, so the marketplace-facing overview and the walkthrough project have nothing to learn.

No `src/` production file changes (`D40`'s boundary and `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2`): the product CLI does not gain a record verb, `D40` step (2b) is not started, and no lint issue code is added (`D40` step (3) is not started).
